reviews.summary: One fix: 'Which of us would win a game show, and which one?' was ambiguous read aloud. Polish: neutral proposal wording, 'till' is UK-only, say Fortune Cookie is a paid template.

dealbreakers: A claim about Ethos that the files don't support. The post says How well do you know me? 'turns the "things you might not know" questions into a quiz'. The game uses its own eight fixed questions, each with four answers to pick from (messages/en.json games.know.blurb and listIntro; KNOW_QUESTIONS in src/lib/games/content). It does not use the post's questions. The same claim appears in the ES version.
reviews.summary: The know-me game claim was wrong (it has its own eight questions); the Gottman paraphrase added 'notice the gaps' and 'kept up to date', which the page doesn't say; nine Spanish lines were calques or changed the meaning (perdonaran, matrimonio de tus padres, de qué quieres más, temporada callada, concurso, hacer las paces, word order, ponerse al día, guapa).
Two People-also-ask questions from the variants were unanswered: 'Why does my husband listen to everyone but me?' and 'How to reduce husband stress?'. Add them in both languages.

reviews.summary: Round-one fixes made correctly. Better than the top results because it pairs 101 questions sorted by stage with how to ask them: go-first lines, a weekly check-in and what to do with one-word answers.

All round-one fixes verified against the code. One fix: '¿De qué te arrepientes pero ya lo tienes asumido?' is ungrammatical. Polish: vosotros/tú switch in the Gottman line, 'versión en test', 'lo que quiere ahora' vs 'next', and a few idioms.
Every People-also-ask question is now answered; the stage table, go-first openers, weekly check-in and one-word-answers section give more than The Knot, marriage.com and Paired.

reviews.summary: The page to send a friend: 101 questions that move from nostalgic to deep to flirty, a table for choosing by marriage stage, and concrete lines to borrow.

Every product claim matches the code and every link resolves; it beats the top results because its questions are written for years into a marriage (what's changed, a weekly check-in, one-word answers), not a generic list.
No top page has the stage table, the go-first openers or the one-word-answers section, and the FAQ answers every People-also-ask question across the main, deep and fun variants.
